title: Constant Acceleration of Falling Bodies
description: Covers Galileo's discovery that all bodies, regardless of their mass, accelerate towards the Earth with a constant acceleration.

title: Kepler's Laws
description: Introduces the three elegant laws derived by Johannes Kepler that describe the motion of planets.

title: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation
description: Presents the foundational law proposed by Newton explaining the universal attraction between all massive objects.

title: Law of Orbits
description: All planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun situated at one of the foci of the ellipse.

title: Law of Areas
description: The line that joins any planet to the sun sweeps equal areas in equal intervals of time.

title: Law of Periods
description: The square of the time period of revolution of a planet is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis of the ellipse traced out by the planet.

title: Universal Law of Gravitation
description: Every body in the universe attracts every other body with a force directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them, mathematically expressed as F = G * m1 * m2 / r^2.

title: Newton's Third Law of Motion (for Gravity)
description: Gravitational forces between two bodies are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, meaning the force on body 1 due to body 2 is equal and opposite to the force on body 2 due to body 1 (F₁₂ = -F₂₁).

title: Principle of Superposition for Gravitational Forces
description: The total gravitational force on any body due to a collection of other bodies is the vector sum of the gravitational forces exerted individually by each of the other bodies.

title: Gravitational Force of a Spherical Shell (External Point)
description: The force of attraction between a hollow spherical shell of uniform density and a point mass situated outside is as if the entire mass of the shell is concentrated at its center.

title: Gravitational Force of a Spherical Shell (Internal Point)
description: The force of attraction due to a hollow spherical shell of uniform density on a point mass situated inside it is zero.

title: Universal Law of Gravitation
description: This fundamental law describes the attractive force between any two objects with mass, proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers, involving the gravitational constant G.

title: The Cavendish Experiment
description: This experimental setup, first used by Henry Cavendish, precisely measures the Universal Gravitational Constant (G) by observing the torsion twist caused by the gravitational attraction between large and small lead spheres.

title: Principle of Torque Equilibrium in Torsion Balance
description: In the Cavendish experiment, the gravitational torque exerted by the large spheres on the small spheres is balanced by the restoring torque of the twisted suspension wire at equilibrium, allowing G to be calculated.

title: Gravitational Force Outside a Spherical Body
description: Explains that the gravitational force exerted by a spherical body on an external point mass is equivalent to its entire mass being concentrated at its center.

title: Gravitational Force Inside a Spherical Body
description: Explains that for a point inside a uniform spherical body, only the mass of the sphere within the point's radius from the center contributes to the gravitational force.

title: Acceleration Due to Gravity (g) at Earth's Surface
description: Describes the derivation of the acceleration due to gravity 'g' at the Earth's surface by equating gravitational force with Newton's Second Law.

title: Newton’s Second Law of Motion
description: States the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration ($F=mg$), which is used to define acceleration due to gravity.

title: Acceleration Due to Gravity Above Earth's Surface
description: This concept covers the derivation and formula for the acceleration experienced by a mass at a height 'h' above the Earth's surface, showing how it decreases with increasing distance from the Earth's center.

title: Approximation for Acceleration at Small Heights
description: This concept explains the approximation of the acceleration due to gravity for small heights 'h' above the Earth's surface using binomial expansion, revealing a linear decrease.

title: Acceleration Due to Gravity Below Earth's Surface
description: This concept covers the derivation and formula for the acceleration due to gravity at a depth 'd' below the Earth's surface, demonstrating its linear decrease as one approaches the center.

title: Gravitational Potential Energy (Constant Gravity)
description: Explains the calculation of potential energy `mgh` when the gravitational force is assumed constant near the Earth's surface.

title: Work Done by Variable Gravitational Force
description: Details the calculation of work done by the gravitational force using integration when the force varies with distance according to the inverse-square law.

title: Gravitational Potential Energy (General Form)
description: Establishes the general formula `U = -GMm/r` for gravitational potential energy between two masses, conventionally setting potential energy to zero at infinite separation.

title: Gravitational Potential
description: Defines gravitational potential as the gravitational potential energy per unit mass at a given point due to a gravitational field.

title: Gravitational Potential Energy of Multi-Particle Systems
description: Describes how to calculate the total gravitational potential energy for a system of multiple particles by summing the potential energies of all possible pairs using the superposition principle.

title: Principle of Conservation of Energy
description: This principle states that the total mechanical energy (sum of kinetic and potential energy) of an object remains constant in the absence of non-conservative forces.

title: Concept of Escape Speed
description: The minimum initial speed an object needs to completely overcome the gravitational pull of a celestial body and achieve an infinite distance with zero kinetic energy.

title: Derivation of Escape Speed
description: The process of applying the principle of conservation of energy to an object initially near a celestial body and finally at infinity to deduce the escape speed formula.

title: Formulas for Escape Speed
description: The specific mathematical expressions for calculating escape speed, including forms dependent on the gravitational constant, mass and radius of the body, and its surface gravity.

title: Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion
description: Explains that Kepler's laws, which describe planetary motion, are equally applicable to Earth satellites, dictating their circular or elliptic orbits.

title: Centripetal Force in Orbital Motion
description: Defines the centripetal force required to keep a satellite in a circular orbit around the Earth.

title: Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation
description: Explains that the centripetal force required for a satellite's orbit is provided by the gravitational force exerted by the Earth.

title: Orbital Velocity and Period Derivation
description: Demonstrates how equating the centripetal and gravitational forces allows for the derivation of a satellite's orbital velocity and its corresponding time period.

title: Kepler's Law of Periods for Satellites
description: Derives and applies Kepler's Third Law, known as the Law of Periods, to describe the relationship between a satellite's orbital period and its orbital radius around Earth.

title: Kinetic Energy in Orbit
description: This concept covers the derivation and calculation of the kinetic energy of a satellite moving in a circular orbit, based on its orbital speed and mass.

title: Gravitational Potential Energy
description: This concept explains the calculation of the gravitational potential energy of an orbiting satellite at a given distance from Earth, with the reference point of zero potential energy at infinity.

title: Total Mechanical Energy of Orbiting Satellite
description: This concept defines the total mechanical energy of a satellite as the sum of its kinetic and potential energies, highlighting its specific characteristics for both circular and elliptic orbits.

title: Energy and Orbital Stability
description: This concept explains the critical relationship between the total mechanical energy of a celestial body and the nature of its trajectory, distinguishing between bound orbits (negative total energy) and escape trajectories (zero or positive total energy).
